# select_alert_integration (Resource)

Enables an email or MS Teams webhook alert integration for the organization. An organization has at most one integration of each type. When one is already enabled, create adopts it. Destroy disables the integration for the full organization, and SELECT refuses it while the integration has destinations. A Slack integration needs a browser sign-in: connect it in the SELECT UI and use the `select_alert_integration` data source.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Destroying this resource disables email alerts for the full organization.
resource "select_alert_integration" "email" {
  integration_type = "email"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `integration_type` (String) `email` or `ms_teams_webhook`. Changing it forces a new integration.

### Read-Only

- `create_time` (String) When the integration was connected — RFC 3339 UTC.
- `credentials_configured` (Boolean) Whether SELECT holds credentials for this integration.
- `display_name` (String) The integration's name, as SELECT shows it.
- `etag` (String) Opaque strong ETag for this integration. Sent as `If-Match` on deletes.
- `id` (String) The integration's identifier in SELECT. Use it with `terraform import`.
- `status` (String) The status of SELECT's connection: `unknown`, `pending`, `failing` or `connected`.
- `update_time` (String) When the integration was last changed — RFC 3339 UTC.

## Import

`select_alert_integration` can be imported with the integration type and the integration's ID in SELECT:

```bash
terraform import select_alert_integration.email email/2f1c8b4e-9a6d-4d1f-9d0e-7d3a5b6c8e01
```

The import fails when the integration is not of the given type. Usually an import is not necessary: a create adopts the organization's existing integration.
